prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1220; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the impact occurred as the insured described and admitted fault for following too closely. Police report obtained and lists the claimant as an occupant of the striking vehicle.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos from the scene and the insured's own images; the rear bumper damage and the trunk lid deformation are largely consistent with the reported impact speed. No prior damage to this vehicle is on file.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the sequence of events described by both drivers. Neither witness had any connection to the parties involved.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact. The injury pattern is consistent with bracing against the dashboard or wheel during a collision of this force, and no prior injury to that wrist or arm appears in the records requested.

Entry 6: Medical records received from the treating facility show a standard course of care: immobilization, a follow-up orthopedic visit, and physical therapy. Treatment tapered as the claimant's range of motion improved.

Entry 7: Counsel's office provided a written summary of the claimant's account. It matches the recorded statement given earlier and the description given at the scene, with no material differences in the sequence or details.

Entry 8: Confirmed with the policy file that the driver of the insured vehicle lives in the policyholder's household and is listed as a covered household member. Coverage was in force on the loss date, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 9: Medical bills and the repair estimate have been reviewed against the damage described. Charges are in line with usual rates for the treatment provided, and the repair scope matches the visible damage in the photos.

Entry 10: Follow-up with counsel scheduled to request the complete imaging file and the physical therapy notes. No additional documentation issues identified at this stage.

Entry 11: File remains open pending receipt of the remaining records and the final repair invoice. Reserve reviewed and maintained at the current level until treatment is confirmed complete.
